For a baby who **leaks at night**, the best starting move is usually:

**Buy the Snug-Fit Overnight Diaper one size larger than your baby’s daytime diaper** — *as long as it still fits snugly at the legs and waist with no gaps.* Sizing up often helps because the larger diaper has more absorbent capacity; Pampers also notes that consistent leaking can mean baby needs a different size or more absorbency. ([support.pampers.com](https://support.pampers.com/hc/en-us/articles/21678052813597-How-can-I-prevent-diaper-leakage-and-protect-my-baby-s-skin))

**Quick guide:**
- Daytime **Size 2** → try overnight **Size 3**
- Daytime **Size 3** → try overnight **Size 4**
- Daytime **Size 4** → try overnight **Size 5**
- Daytime **Size 5** → try overnight **Size 6**

If the bigger size leaves **leg gaps**, don’t use it—gaps cause leaks. In that case, stay in the current size and try a **diaper booster pad** or a different overnight brand/cut. Overnight leak guides commonly recommend sizing up, but specifically warn not to size up if it creates gaps. ([albeebaby.com](https://www.albeebaby.com/blogs/from-the-cradle/overnight-diaper-leaks))

Also check fit before bed:
- Leg ruffles/cuffs pulled fully out
- Tabs snug, not loose
- Waistband not gapping
- For boys, point penis downward before fastening

If you tell me your baby’s **weight** and current diaper size, I can give you the exact size to buy.
